To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an outbreak of viral hepatitis B (n = 39) and C (n = 8) occurred in patients treated at an oncological hospital in Slovakia.
an outbreak of hepatitis B and C was caused by the reuse of disposable materials for parenteral treatment of patients.
the outbreak of hepatitis B and C was related to the use of disposable materials for parenteral treatment in the oncology ward.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of the use of disposable materials and the importance of the implementation of standard procedures.
the risk of nosocomial infections and their prevention in oncological departments.
the epidemiological investigation of a viral hepatitis B and hepatitis C outbreak in patients with cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the outbreak was related to parenteral treatments at the oncological ward.
there is a risk of infection in patients who received parenteral treatment in the oncology department.
the outbreak of viral hepatitis B/C at the oncological department was caused by improper parenteral treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no need to change the current practice of using disposable materials in oncology wards, but it is necessary to improve adherence to standard procedures and to train staff in this regard.
the outbreak of hepatitis B and C was caused by the lack of adherence to standard procedures and by a failure of the quality assurance system in a hospital.
it is necessary to improve the knowledge of health care professionals in order to prevent nosocomial transmission of bloodborne viruses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of transmission of infectious disease in a hospital is not only related to the use of reusable medical devices, but is also dependent on the adherence to the standard procedures.
it is important to be aware of the risks of nosocomial transmission and the need to improve the quality of care in hospitals.
the risk of bloodborne infections in hospitals is still present and can be prevented by adherence to the standard precautions and the use of disposable material.
